idiom_name: fun interface + SAM conversion for single-method commands; sealed interface with when for data commands
implementation_notes: Kotlin removes the single-method command class through functional interfaces: a fun interface plus SAM conversion lets a lambda be the implementation, which kotlinlang documents explicitly as the replacement for 'a class that implements a functional interface manually', and ArrayDeque serves as the history. For undo, logging and replay the idiomatic shape is data-oriented - a sealed interface with data classes per request and an exhaustive when over it, so the compiler proves every command is handled and requests stay immutable, comparable values; named classes remain appropriate when a command owns private state and its own inverse.
pitfalls: SAM conversion covers fun interfaces and Java interfaces, not a two-method command: execute plus undo needs a real type, or two lambdas grouped in a data class.
A lambda command has no identity or label, so logging, deduplication and replay require a data class or an explicit id alongside it.
when over a sealed hierarchy is exhaustive only within the module that declares it - adding a subtype elsewhere is a compile error by design, so keep command hierarchies with their interpreter.
